# WealthSprout

> WealthSprout publishes age-matched financial literacy workbooks for kids and teens, ages 5–18. Each program is a digital PDF, sold as a one-time purchase (no subscription), covering topics school doesn't teach: saving, budgeting, compound interest, stocks, index funds, Roth IRAs, credit, and taxes.

WealthSprout is a children's financial education company, not a financial advisor — products are educational workbooks for families, not investment advice.

## Programs

- [My First Money Kit](https://www.wealthsprout.com/free-kit): Free 12-page PDF for ages 5–10. Introduces the 3-Jar System (Spend/Save/Give) and a first savings goal worksheet. $0, instant delivery, no credit card.
- [Wealth Blueprint](https://www.wealthsprout.com/programs/wealth-blueprint): $29 one-time. 60-page workbook for ages 13–15 covering stocks, index funds, Roth IRAs, side hustles, and basic real estate investing.
- [Launch Rich](https://www.wealthsprout.com/programs/launch-rich): $34 one-time. 70-page workbook for ages 16–18 covering credit scores, filing taxes, first-paycheck investing, 401(k) matches, salary negotiation, and student loans.
- [The WealthSprout Vault](https://www.wealthsprout.com/programs/vault): $67 one-time. Bundle of all four paid programs (Money Seeds, Money Moves, Wealth Blueprint, Launch Rich) plus the free kit and a bonus Family Money Conversation Guide. Retail value $104.

Two additional age-matched programs — Money Seeds (ages 5–8, $17) and Money Moves (ages 9–12, $24) — are sold from the homepage product grid at https://www.wealthsprout.com/#programs.

## Key facts

- All products are instantly-delivered PDF downloads, usable on any device or printable at home.
- Every paid program includes a parent guide; no financial background is required to use them with a child.
- One-time payment only — there is no subscription tier.
- 30-day money-back guarantee on all paid programs.
- Support: hello@wealthsproutkids.com
